content.text: {"primary_meaning":"In Christian teaching and biblical interpretation, the cloud is most commonly understood as a symbol of the divine presence and glory of God (often called the Shekinah glory) — the visible manifestation of God's presence that simultaneously reveals and conceals Him, guiding, protecting, and accompanying His people, and associated with theophany and, in the New Testament, with Christ's ascension and return.","primary_basis":["Exodus 13:21-22 (pillar of cloud guiding Israel)","Exodus 16:10 (glory of the LORD appearing in the cloud)","Exodus 19:9, 16 (cloud at Sinai theophany)","Exodus 24:15-18 (cloud covering the mountain; glory of the LORD)","Exodus 33:9-10 (pillar of cloud at the tent of meeting)","Exodus 40:34-38 (cloud filling the tabernacle)","Leviticus 16:2 (God appearing in the cloud over the mercy seat)","Numbers 9:15-23 (cloud directing Israel's journeys)","1 Kings 8:10-11 (cloud filling Solomon's temple)","Psalm 97:2; Psalm 104:3 (clouds surrounding God; clouds as His chariot)","Ezekiel 1:4; 10:3-4 (cloud in visions of God's glory)","Daniel 7:13 (Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven)","Matthew 17:5; Mark 9:7; Luke 9:34-35 (bright cloud at the Transfiguration)","Matthew 24:30; 26:64 (Son of Man coming on the clouds)","Acts 1:9-11 (cloud receiving Christ at the ascension)","1 Thessalonians 4:17 (caught up in the clouds)","Revelation 1:7; 14:14 (Christ coming with/on the clouds)","1 Corinthians 10:1-2 (Israel baptized 'in the cloud')"],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Eschatological judgment and the Day of the LORD — clouds as imagery of darkness, dread, and impending divine judgment.","basis":["Joel 2:2","Zephaniah 1:15","Ezekiel 30:3","Isaiah 19:1","Nahum 1:3"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"A great multitude — the 'cloud of witnesses' as a metaphor for a vast crowd of faithful believers.","basis":["Hebrews 12:1"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Transience and fleetingness — clouds that quickly vanish as a picture of short-lived devotion, life, or sin removed.","basis":["Hosea 6:4; 13:3","Job 7:9; 30:15","Isaiah 44:22 (sins blotted out like a cloud)","James 4:14 (mist/vapor imagery, related)"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Emptiness and false promise — 'clouds without rain/water' as a figure for boastful or false teachers who deliver nothing.","basis":["Jude 12","2 Peter 2:17","Proverbs 25:14"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Divine concealment, hiddenness, and mystery — the cloud as that which veils God from human sight, developed especially in mystical/apophatic tradition (e.g., 'The Cloud of Unknowing').","basis":["Exodus 20:21 (thick darkness where God was)","1 Kings 8:12","Lamentations 3:44","Job 22:13-14","Psalm 18:11"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Blessing, rain, and divine provision — clouds as bearers of rain signifying God's favor and refreshment.","basis":["1 Kings 18:44-45","Deuteronomy 33:26-28","Psalm 147:8","Zechariah 10:1"],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":true,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is broad, well-attested agreement across Catholic, Orthodox, Protestant, and academic biblical scholarship that the cloud's primary symbolic meaning is the manifest presence and glory of God (Shekinah), a theme that runs coherently from the Exodus narratives through the Transfiguration, Ascension, and Second Coming texts. The alternative meanings listed are genuinely present in Scripture and interpretation but are context-specific figures rather than rivals to the dominant theophany/glory reading. The 'cloud of witnesses' usage in Hebrews 12:1 is widely recognized but is a distinct idiom (a crowd metaphor), not the core symbolic tradition."}
